related_questions.question: Are my old COVID test kits still good?

text_blocks.snippet: Expired COVID-19 test kits are not recommended for use, as their accuracy may be compromised. While some tests, particularly lateral flow or rapid antigen tests, might still provide a valid result for a limited time past their expiration date, this is not guaranteed. If you have an expired test, it's best to check the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (.gov) website for potential extended expiration dates. If the test is significantly expired or if the test result doesn't appear as expected (e.g., the line(s) do not appear in the correct location or time), a new test should be used for accurate results.

list.title: Expiration Dates Matter:
list.snippet: COVID-19 test kits have expiration dates printed on the packaging, and these dates are crucial for ensuring accurate results.

list.title: Potential for Inaccuracy:
list.snippet: After the expiration date, the chemicals and materials within the test kit can degrade, potentially leading to inaccurate results.

list.title: Checking for Extended Expiration:
list.snippet: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (.gov) website may provide information about extended expiration dates for certain tests.

list.title: When to Replace:
list.snippet: If a test is expired, it's generally recommended to replace it with a new one.

list.title: If You Must Use an Expired Test:
list.snippet: If you must use an expired test, carefully review the instructions and be aware that the results may not be reliable. If the test doesn't perform as expected (e.g., the line(s) do not appear correctly or within the specified time), discard it and use a new test.
